\caption{Secondary results per penalty, task and decoder (definitions in Supplementary Note 7; all descriptive). HV: hypervolume up to the highest common batch score (Figure 4), the area of the batch-score by biology-score plane reached by the penalty's sweep points beyond the reference point (plain scVI's batch score, plain scVI's biology score minus 0.10), with batch scores above the highest common batch score counted at it, divided by the batch gap that sets $b^*$; HV$_{\mathrm{all}}$: the same without that cap, so that batch removal beyond the highest common batch score adds area; n/a in low-signal pairs. Non-dom.: strengths that no other strength of the penalty beats on both scores, of all its strengths. Coll.\ all: number of fits $n$ (30, 33 or 36: all strengths times three seeds) and the percentage that failed or lost 0.10 or more biology against the same seed's plain scVI, with the exact (Clopper--Pearson) 95\% interval, which is nominal because the fits of one seed share one threshold; 0 fits diverged or had a non-finite latent, so every collapse is a loss of biology. $n_{\mathrm{c}}$ and Coll.\ common: the same for the fits at strengths whose mean batch score is at most the highest common batch score (the range of Figure 4 and of the main-text collapse rate, Figure 5). \textbf{Part B}: low-signal pairs, shown for completeness and left out of every summary that uses $b^*$ (Supplementary Note 5).}\label{tab:s8}\\
